teaser.text: Alibaba is chiefly a digital marketplace operator: it connects shoppers and businesses, then sells the computing, logistics and retail services that help those transactions happen. Its money comes from fees, service charges and some direct sales, while its costs come from technology, people, inventory, infrastructure and delivery.

blocks.heading: What has to go right—and wrong for Alibaba?

paragraphs.text: AI workloads grow too slowly to fill new infrastructure, while subsidies, delivery costs and AI application losses suppress margins. Dilution continues because buybacks remain suspended. The shares fall from HKD57.61 in October 2027 to HKD48.45 in October 2029. Its 31% probability reflects risks already visible in falling China E-commerce adjusted EBITA, negative free cash flow and June capex above operating cash flow.

The bull case requires paid AI demand, high capacity utilization, narrower AI losses and better delivery economics at the same time. Buybacks then amplify per-share earnings, and investors award a higher multiple. The shares rise from HKD145.77 to HKD273.75. Its 20% probability reflects credible growth evidence but no established group-level cash return from the programme.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Alibaba really make?

paragraphs.text: Capital spending, or capex, is cash invested in long-lived assets such as servers, data centres and equipment. Alibaba’s infrastructure spending turned operating cash flow into negative free cash flow in FY2026. Its own free-cash-flow definition is less negative because it excludes some capital expenditures and makes specified adjustments.

A further owner-focused measure deducts stock compensation as an economic cost, even though it is not another cash payment. The same discipline prevents double-counting lease payments, interest or working-capital movements.

blocks.heading: How much does Alibaba pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The forecast uses CNY0.90 per share in every case and every period. This approximates the declared regular dividend of US$0.13125, which has been stable since FY2023. FY2026 free cash flow was negative CNY50,724 million, so the model excludes the prior year’s extraordinary dividend and assumes infrastructure spending limits increases.

blocks.heading: Does Alibaba’s cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is the cash left after operating cash pays for capital expenditure. Alibaba’s free cash flow turned negative in FY2026 because investment spending exceeded the cash generated by operations. Dividends and buybacks then consumed still more money, leaving less for new projects.

earnings.meta_description: Alibaba’s next results are expected on December 1, 2026; guidance centers on AI revenue, with demand turning investment into cash as the key test.
earnings.opening: Alibaba’s next results are expected on December 1, 2026. The key thing to watch is whether external demand fills capacity and turns cloud investment into cash.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how Alibaba’s business works, who its rivals are, how management operates and what risks could change the outcome.

blocks.heading: What has Alibaba guided for AI products and cloud?

paragraphs.text: Management has guided to a US$10 billion annualized AI-product revenue run rate in the quarter ending September 2026. Annualized means multiplying the latest quarter’s pace by four; it is not money already collected. If Taobao, which Alibaba owns, uses Alibaba Cloud, that may prove the technology’s value, but money moving between Alibaba divisions is not new revenue for the consolidated group.

The larger promise is to exceed US$100 billion in annual combined external cloud and AI revenue within five years. It includes ordinary computing, storage and databases, not only model services. Management also maintains a calendar-year-end target of RMB30 billion in annual recurring revenue from model and application services, including model as a service, through which customers use hosted models instead of running their own systems.

blocks.heading: What are Alibaba’s recent revenue and profit trends?

paragraphs.text: June 2026 brought higher sales but much weaker profitability. Revenue rose, while gross margin, operating income, net income and diluted EPS all fell sharply.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Alibaba’s next results?

paragraphs.text: The decisive evidence will be paying customers, repeatable merchant returns and regulatory execution. September-quarter results should test the annualized AI-product milestone, while December-quarter disclosures should test the model-and-application-services target.

Investors should track external cloud sales, margins, capital spending and free cash flow together. Alibaba separates AI Cloud and Compute Services from AI Labs and Applications, allowing a basic question: are infrastructure sales becoming profitable enough to support the continuing cost of developing and distributing models?
